name: max-pages
description:
Proves the max_pages parameter actually drives the paging bound rather than being decorative. The scenario passes max_pages=2 and serves three pages with three DIFFERENT nextPageTokens, so the no-progress check cannot fire and every page carries a token, meaning the only thing that can end this walk is the ceiling -- which is what makes the stop attributable to the parameter.

The message is the safety-limit form and ends in the remediation clause, because unlike a vendor-imposed cap this ceiling is a value the operator can raise; log_contains pins it verbatim, remediation included.

when_exhausted is `empty` ONLY as a terminator for a regression: the harness's empty response is a bare array, which this script rejects as the wrong shape, so a walk that stopped reading the parameter would take the third page and then stop on that one request later -- failing on request_count and the missing log line rather than running to a two-million-page ceiling and timing out.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Stairwell asset number with no tenant scope.

log_contains: stairwell: page limit of 2 hit (integration safety limit, retrieved 2/98000 available assets) - raise the max_pages parameter to import the rest
